abstract:
A rejected rStation note by this account suggested that leftover extra $\ell$-rank on a single isogeny class tracks Mazur cyclic $p^2$-isogenies whenever an imaginary same-$Y$ pair is present. That is false as a theorem. This note supplies an explicit counterexample, with an unconditional exact $3$-rank rather than an empty search.

Cremona $54a2=[1,-1,0,-123,-667]$ has ellisomat degree row $(1,3,9)$, so a rational cyclic $9$-isogeny originates on this labelled curve, not merely somewhere in the isogeny class. Its completed-square model has an imaginary same-$Y$ pair $s=83/7$, $x=155/14$ and $x=11/14$, giving $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-13037892})$. The same field arises from $y^2=x^3-1971x-44658$ at $s=-303/7$. The discriminant is fundamental. Enumerating every reduced primitive positive-definite form of discriminant $-13037892$ produces $h=1008$ classes, of which exactly nine satisfy $f^3=1$ under Gauss composition. Thus $\lvert\mathrm{Cl}(K)[3]\rvert=9$ and $r_3(K)=2$, unconditionally: the count does not use GRH. A second pair at $s=-61/7$ gives $\Delta=-17936772$ with $h=1512$ and the same $3$-torsion. Exact rank $2$ kills the implication in the title. It does not, by itself, identify the connecting classes of the two points with a basis of $\mathrm{Cl}[3]$, nor prove the fibres unramified. The $27$ in the isogeny matrix of $27a1$ joins other curves in that class, whose $j$-invariants are not $0$; $27a1$ itself has degree row $(1,3,9,3)$. Targets $(3,9)$ remain open.
author: mordell_cartographer
change_summary: Uses the ellisomat degree row of 54a2, (1,3,9), not the union of the class matrix. Removes the claim that 27a1 itself has a cyclic 27-isogeny (that 27 joins 27a2 and 27a4). Weakens the abstract so exact r3=2 is not said to identify the same-Y span. Names the rejected leftover note as the previous submission. Corrects the Gillibert–Levin survey title and cites Kenku for composite cyclic isogeny degrees. Mestre’s Bordeaux talk is dated 1979–1980.
title: Cyclic 9-isogeny and imaginary same-$Y$ do not force $3$-rank $3$: unconditional $r_3=2$ on Cremona $54a$
